{{Short description|Greek philosopher and theologian}}
'''Georgios Sougdouris''' ({{langx|el|Γεώργιος Σουγδουρής}}; 1645/7–1725) was a [[Greeks|Greek]] philosopher and theologian.

==Biography==
Sougdouris was born in [[Ioannina]] then part of the [[Ottoman Empire]], where he finished ground level studies. He continued his studies at the [[University of Venice]] and in [[Padua]] where he may have attended courses at the [[University of Padua|local university]].<ref name=Hellinomnimon>{{cite web|title=Σουγδουρής Γεώργιος [μέσα 17ου αι., Ιωάννινα - 1725, Ιωάννινα]|url=http://195.134.75.14/hellinomnimon/authors//Sougdouris.html|work=University of Athens Database|publisher=Hellinomnimon|accessdate=30 June 2011}}</ref> In 1681, Sougdouris became a priest. Two years later, he became the head of the {{Interlanguage link multi|Goumas School|el|3=Σχολή Εμμανουήλ Γκιούμα}} in Ioannina (a.k.a. Gioumeios or Gioumas School), succeeding [[Bessarion Makris]]. There, he taught natural sciences, mathematics and [[Aristotelian philosophy]].<ref name=Hellinomnimon/> Sougdouris taught at the Goumas school until 1710, and was succeeded by [[Methodios Anthrakites]].<ref name=arapopoulou>{{cite book|last=Maria Arapopoulou, Maria Chritē|first=ed. by A.-F. Christidis|title=A history of ancient Greek: from the beginnings to late antiquity|year=2007|publisher=Cambridge Univ. Press|location=Cambridge [u.a.]|isbn=978-0-521-83307-3|pages=1248|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WJbd0m6YaFkC&pg=PA1248 |edition=1. publ.}}</ref> He wrote a number of philological, theological and philosophical works like ''Εισαγωγή Λογική'' (Introduction to Logic), published in Vienna, 1792 and ''Επιτομή Γραμματικής'' (Concise Grammar), both were extensively used as school textbooks.<ref name=Hellinomnimon/><ref name=arapopoulou/> Moreover, he translated into Greek the work of [[Francesco Panigarola]] ''Rhetorica Ecclesiastica''.<ref name=Hellinomnimon/>

Sougdouris got involved in various theological discussions with local scholars.<ref>{{cite book|title=Ostkirchliche Studien, Vol. 24-25|year=1975|publisher=Augustinus-Verlag|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_DHZAAAAMAAJ&q=sougdouris%2Benergie}}</ref> Due to his progressive views and teaching methods, he got into conflict with conservative circles and was accused of atheism.<ref>{{cite web|last=Δερματά|first=Φωτεινή|title=Νεοελληνικός Διαφωτισμός και η Ήπειρος [Greek Enlightenment and Epirus]|url=http://www.zosimaia.gr/?page=article&id=78|work=zosimaia.gr|publisher=Σύλλογος Αποφοίτων Ζωσιμαίας Σχολής Ιωαννίνων|accessdate=4 July 2011}}</ref> As a result, the local Orthodox bishop asked for Sougdouris' excommunication but failed.<ref name=Nicolaidis>{{cite book|last=Nicolaidis|first=[edited by] Ekmeleddin Ihsanoglu, Kostas Chatzis, Efthymios|title=Multicultural science in the Ottoman empire: the XXth International Congress of History of Science was organized by th Belgian National Committee for Logic, History and Philosophy of Science|year=2003|publisher=Brepols|location=Turnhout|isbn=978-2-503-51446-8 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FQwXAQAAMAAJ&q=%22One+such+instance+was+the+case+of+Georgios+Soug-+douris%2C+who+became+headmaster+of+the+Giouma+School+in+Ioannina+in+1683.+This+Italy-educated+scholar+introduced+exact+sciences+in+the+school+and+systematically+taught+Philosophy+using+new+methods%2C+%22+causing+a+storm+of+protest+.+The+bishop+of+Ioannina+at+that+time%2C+Klimis%2C+asked+for+the+scholar%27s+excommunication+because+Sougdouris+was+not+thinking+according+to+divine+%22 |edition=null |page=56}}</ref>
